newsitem.title: POLAND: Six MPs quit Poland's centrist Union for Freedom.
newsitem.headline: Six MPs quit Poland's centrist Union for Freedom.

text.p: Six deputies have quit Poland's largest parliamentary opposition party, the Union for Freedom (UW), and one of them said on Wednesday the grouping had no chance of victory in this year's elections.
The six plan to join a new party that will be in a centre-right opposition alliance gathered around the Solidarity trade union, the Solidarity Election Action (AWS).

Recent opinion polls have suggested that the AWS, with about 20 percent support, could beat the ruling ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) in parliamentary elections late this year, while the UW is trailing both with about 10 percent.

"In my opinion the UW doesn't have any chance of victory against the SLD, and also cannot form a wide centre-right alliance because it is an elitist party," one of the members who resigned, Bronislaw Komorowski, told reporters.
The Union for Freedom groups some of the intellectuals who advised Solidarity during its fight for democracy, then steered Poland's economic reforms after the 1989 fall of communism.

But it is now estranged from its former allies in the Solidarity union and internally strained by tension between its left and right wings. The defectors, including prominent politician Jan Maria Rokita, came from the party's right.
UW leader Leszek Balcerowicz called on Wednesday for the six to resign their parliamentary seats.
